subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Should shared OAuth refresh perform bounded retries across providers, and which error classes and maximum added latency are acceptable?
rationale: The implementation shape is clear, but choosing retryable failures and the lock-compatible latency budget affects every OAuth provider and cannot be safely inferred from one Anthropic incident.

options.title: Adopt classified shared retries
options.body: Retry only typed transient network, timeout, 408, 429, and retryable 5xx failures with jitter and a strict total latency cap.

options.title: Keep retries provider-owned
options.body: Require each provider refresh adapter to define its own retry policy and leave the shared manager single-shot.

options.title: Keep single-shot refresh
options.body: Decline refresh retries and rely on credential adoption, profile fallback, clearer diagnostics, and reauthentication recovery.

recommendation.title: Adopt classified shared retries
recommendation.body: Retry only typed transient network, timeout, 408, 429, and retryable 5xx failures with jitter and a strict total latency cap.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history is most directly connected to the current shared OAuth lifecycle and its cross-provider recovery boundaries.
